wu: Timeline Interviews: Students draw a personal timeline from birth to now with 5 key life events. In pairs, they ask 'How long have you lived in Oujda?' and 'How long have you studied English?' using for/since.
wuAlt: For/Since Chain: Students stand in a circle. One student says 'I have lived in Morocco for 10 years.' The next says 'I have studied English since 2020,' and so on, building a chain.
National Milestones Quiz: Show flashcards of Moroccan events (Green March, Independence). Students guess the year and make a sentence with 'for' or 'since'.
pres: Present perfect + for/since is introduced using a Green March timeline (1975-present). Model sentences: 'Morocco has had the Sahara since 1975.' 'We have celebrated the Green March for 48 years.' Check understanding with thumbs up/down for true/false sentences about the timeline.
presAlt: Realia Display: Bring in Moroccan currency or a map. Point to the Sahara and say 'Morocco has controlled this area since 1975.' Students repeat and make their own sentences about national symbols.
Video Clip: Show a 1-min clip of the Green March. Pause to ask 'How long have Moroccans remembered this event?' and elicit 'since 1975'.
prac: For-Since Sorting Relay: Divide into 2 teams. Give each team a set of cards (time expressions: '5 years', '2018', 'last month', 'ages') and sentence starters ('I have worked here...', 'He has lived here...'). Teams race to sort cards into 'for' or 'since' columns on the board.
pracAlt: How-Long Chains: In groups of 3, students take turns making present perfect sentences with for/since about national achievements (e.g., 'Morocco has hosted CANAFCON since 2023'). The chain continues until someone hesitates.
Sentence Builder: Distribute word cards (I/have/lived/in/Oujda/for/10 years). Students arrange them to make correct sentences, then swap cards with another group.
ls: Listen to short dialogues where people discuss their experiences with for/since (e.g., 'How long have you been a teacher? 'For 5 years.'). Students complete a table with names, jobs, and durations. Check answers by replaying key phrases.
re: Stand Up Sit Down: Call out time expressions (e.g., 'since 2020', 'for a month'). Students stand if it's 'since', sit if it's 'for'. Speed up to make it challenging and fun.
prod: National Milestone Interviews: Students choose a Moroccan milestone (Green March, Independence, etc.). In pairs, they interview each other: 'How long has Morocco celebrated this?' and 'What does it mean for you?' They prepare a 2-minute presentation to share findings.
rw: Read a short article about the Green March. Complete a table with events (e.g., 'Green March', 'Reunification') and durations (e.g., 'since 1975', 'for decades'). Then write 3 sentences about their own experiences using for/since.
st: Play a short clip of a Moroccan song about national unity. End with the goodbye routine: 'Today we learned to describe duration with for and since. Thank you for your participation!'
g: Teams race to place event cards on a timeline, saying sentences like 'Morocco has had the Sahara since 1975'.
Students write 9 time expressions on a grid. Teacher calls out sentences; students mark the matching expression.
Students stand in a circle. Each adds a for/since sentence to the chain, e.g., 'I have lived in Morocco for 20 years. My father has worked here since 1995.'
Students mingle asking 'Find someone who has studied English for more than 2 years' and write names.
Teams bid on correct for/since sentences. Incorrect sentences are 'bought' but don't earn points.
diff: Fast finishers: Write 6 for/since sentences about national milestones.
Support: Use sentence frames like 'Morocco has ______ since ______' and a word bank.
hw: Write 6 sentences about your life experiences using for/since (e.g., 'I have lived in Oujda for 5 years').
Write 6 for/since sentences about national milestones (e.g., 'Morocco has been independent since 1956').
Interview a family member about their experiences with for/since and share 3 sentences in class.
tip: Connect grammar to local history to boost engagement. For example, using the Green March makes 'for/since' meaningful and culturally relevant.
